children.text: Since its debut in 1956, the Rolex Day-Date has stood as the brand's ultimate expression of prestige. Exclusively crafted in precious metals and instantly recognizable by its day display and President bracelet, it has spent decades on the wrists of presidents, business leaders and cultural icons, becoming one of the most enduring symbols of success in watchmaking.

Produced in 1990, this double-quickset 18K white gold ref. 18239 offers an uncommon twist on the classic Day-Date aesthetic. Originally fitted with a silver dial, time has transformed it into a rich tropical brown, creating a unique appearance that could never be replicated intentionally. Combined with its crisp white gold case, fluted bezel and President bracelet, this naturally aged dial gives the watch an individuality that has become increasingly sought-after among collectors.
THE DIAL

Originally finished in silver, the dial has naturally developed a warm tropical brown hue over time. Highly prized by collectors, this organic transformation gives each tropical dial its own unique character while beautifully complementing the cool tones of the 18K white gold case.
THE CONSTRUCTION

Crafted entirely from 18K white gold, the ref. 18239 pairs Rolex's iconic fluted bezel with the unmistakable President bracelet. The monochromatic construction allows the richly aged tropical dial to become the focal point while preserving the Day-Date's timeless elegance.

Watch is in overall excellent condition. The 18K white gold case shows surface scratches and small nicks. The hallmarks and stamps on the rear of the lugs remain crisp. The bezel is in very good condition, with a few more noticeable dings. The dial is excellent, with intact lume plots and a uniform galaxy-esque tropical toffee hue across the surface. It is fitted with a concealed-clasp President bracelet showing surface scratches and moderate play between the links. The bracelet is fitted with 20 links, 1 of which is removable, and fits approximately a 6¾” wrist.

Among vintage and neo-vintage Rolex watches, naturally tropical dials continue to captivate collectors because no two examples age in exactly the same way. This ref. 18239 combines the enduring elegance of the white gold Day-Date with an unusually attractive tropical dial.

children.text: Debuting in 1953 and released to the public the following year, the Rolex Submariner has undoubtedly become one of the most iconic timepieces of all time thanks to its legendary status as Rolex's flagship dive watch. Used extensively by the British Royal Navy and professional diving operations like COMEX, the Submariner set the bar for all dive watches to follow. Featuring a genuinely timeless design that has remained relatively unchanged throughout its history, the Rolex has become the archetypal sports watch. With very few large-scale aesthetic upgrades made to it over the years except for timely advancements like introducing a date function to the collection in the late '60s, and its modern cerachrom bezels, the Submariner is seen as the prototypical dive watch thanks to its consistency. The Submariner has earned its status as a legendary watch, with it today remaining as one of the most sought-after timepieces around.

Released in 2020 to replace the outgoing Rolex Submariner ref. 114060, the ref. 124060 that we have here helped to introduce a number of new elements to the Submariner's pure and heritage-consistent "No-Date" collection. Additionally, the 40mm case design of its predecessor and 20mm lug-width have been widened to 41mm and 21mm, respectively, to give the ref. 124060 a wider poise on the wrist. Finally, the ref. 1204060's lugs have been slimmed down to give the watch a more elegant and refined look that moves away from its bulky square design from before. Furthermore, it has been given a new movement so as to step into Rolex’s latest watchmaking standards with its automatic cal. 3230 that now includes 70 hours of power reserve. Furthermore, its hands on its black Maxi-dial have been thickened so as to hold more lume and help with legibility, which points back to the Submariner’s roots as a functional tool watch.
THE DIAL
With its symmetrical time-only display, the Submariner ref. 124060 stays true to the collection's heritage as a utility-oriented dive watch where legibility underwater was Rolex's only concern.
THE CONSTRUCTION
Upgraded to 41mm, the ref. 124060 marked a new era for the Submariner that moved away from the overtly robust design of its predecessor and featured a more elegant poise on the wrist.
TIMING MACHINE READOUT

It is fitted with an Oyster bracelet comprising 12 links, 4 of which are removable, and fits approximately an 8” wrist. A move to modernize the Submariner and give it more elegant proportions closer to those loved by collectors during Rolex's aluminum bezel days, the ref. 124060 is a stunningly beautiful watch that still perfectly stays on task as a tool watch.

children.text: Introduced as a new model in 2020 as Rolex revitalized the entire Oyster Perpetual collection, the Oyster Perpetual 41 features the incredible in-house Rolex cal. 3230 movement within its enlarged 41mm entirely satin-brushed stainless steel case. Featuring 70 hours of power reserve with COSC certification and Rolex's own "Superlative Chronometer" certification, this new movement has ensured that the latest Oyster Perpetuals remain accurate to within -2/+2 seconds a day and feature the same level of horological engineering as any other flagship offering from the Genevan brand. However, keen to keep the collection fresh in the minds of their collectors, Rolex once again revamped the Oyster Perpetual in 2026 by adding to the selection of updated colors that had only launched in 2025, one of which we have here. Offered as a fresh reference, the ref. 134300, this new model is identical to their predecessor in every way besides its dial. Offered here as perhaps the most desirable variant is the Jubilee Motif dial. Inspired by Rolex’s Jubilee motif whereby the word “ROLEX” appears across the entire lacquered dial over and over again, this new take gives the design ten colors that overlap one another to create an incredibly fun and playful spirit. Leaning into the Celebration dial’s colorful design, this Jubilee dial spins the Oyster Perpetual’s subdued aesthetic on its head and creates something entirely new and unusual.

children.text: THE DIAL

Featuring a modern 41mm sizing, the Oyster Perpetual ref. 134300's satin-brushed case exhibits the same sport watch tendencies as the models that it forms the foundation of, like the Submariner, GMT-Master II, and so many others. However, unlike those models, it also retains a refined detail in its polished dome-shaped bezel that none of those models feature.

children.text: Produced during the late 1950s, the Rolex Oyster Precision ref. 6426 represents one of the purest expressions of Rolex’s timeless Oyster. Combining the robust Oyster case with a simple manually wound movement, the model emphasized reliability, legibility, and everyday practicality without unnecessary complication. Watches such as the ref. 6426 formed an important part of Rolex’s catalogue during the period, offering understated sports-watch styling in an accessible and wearable format. Particularly appealing to collectors today are examples fitted with the desirable “3-6-9” dial configuration, whose balanced layout and Arabic numerals evoke the aesthetic language of early Explorer models. The presence of a gilt gloss dial further enhances the vintage charm of the watch, placing it firmly within one of the most admired eras of Rolex dial production.

children.text: THE DIAL

The gilt gloss dial features the highly sought-after “3-6-9” configuration with luminous Arabic numerals and gilt printing that perfectly captures the aesthetic of Rolex sports watches from the late 1950s. Fine spider crazing across the glossy surface adds texture and character to the dial, a trait particularly appreciated by collectors of vintage gilt Rolex watches.
THE CONSTRUCTION
The 34mm Oyster case retains its classic restrained proportions and is fitted with a screw-down Rolex twin-lock crown.

children.text: Released in 2012 as the first new collection in 20 years since the Yacht-Master in 1992, the Sky-Dweller introduced the most complex Rolex movement ever created to the world. Powered by the cal. 9001 movement, the Sky-Dweller features an annual calendar system (called SAROS) requiring only one adjustment a year between February and March, which displays the month by highlighting the corresponding hour marker (8 o’clock is August, 12 is December, and so on) and a GMT function within the ring in the middle of its dial. With an innovative Ring Command System, the Sky-Dweller’s rotating fluted white gold bezel is used to select which of the functions the crown will take control of. Fitted in a 42mm stainless steel case, the ref. 326934 is the most sought-after of the Sky-Dweller variants on the market today, with its steel and white gold construction ensuring it remains as popular and timeless as ever as it blends a wholly functional array of complications with an effortlessly elegant design.
THE ANNUAL CALENDAR

Unlike most annual calendar timepieces, the Sky-Dweller's hour-markers indicate the month corresponding with their position on the dial. January will be highlighted by a red box at 1 o' clock, February at 2 o'clock, March at 3 o'clock, and so on. This example's blue dial shows the month as July in the image above.
THE CONSTRUCTION
Featuring one of Rolex's largest cases, the Sky-Dweller is offered as a 42mm watch but with its polished lugs and fluted white gold bezel, it wears rather elegantly.

The dial and hands remain like new. It is fitted with a solid-link Oyster bracelet showing some surface scratches to the polished centre links and clasp, with no play between the links, and factory stickers still present on the clasp blades. The bracelet is fitted with 12 links, 5 of which are removable, and fits approximately a 7¾” wrist. Comes complete with inner and outer boxes, warranty card, booklet, wallet, and two hangtags.

The most complicated timepiece ever created by Rolex, the Sky-Dweller is already an icon in the contemporary watch-collecting market. Its unique dial and impressive proportions have proven to be exceedingly popular amongst collectors ever since the collection's debut in 2012.

children.text: First released in 1945 in honor of the British RAF following their efforts in WWII, the Air-King has become one of the longest-serving members of Rolex’s catalog, with its official debut as a standalone collection, as we know it today, tracing its origins a little bit more recently to 1958. Since then, the collection has become one of Rolex’s most unique collections, with its design and construction often used as a means to push aesthetic boundaries and experiment with design in a way that few other collections within the Rolex family could. As such, the Air-King collection has been found to sport a vast expanse of dial colors and set-ups, with different bezel configurations and a large variety of sizes.
THE DIAL

Of all the dial variants launched under the Air-King umbrella, this example's silver dial is universally appealing with its applied indices, sword hands, monochromatic color, and impressive legibility.
THE CONSTRUCTION
Featuring the Air-King's no-frills construction, the ref. 5500's aesthetic is defined by its flat polished bezel, lack of crown guards and Rolex's signature Oyster bracelet.
TIMING MACHINE READOUT

The dial shows a couple of light marks on the surface and some aging around the very edge. Some of the lume plots have discoloured, as has the lume in the hands, which also show light scratches. The plastic crystal has a number of scuffs and scratches. The solid link Oyster bracelet has light marks and light play between the links. A Rolex true to the brand's ethos as a tool watchmaker, the Air-King ref. 5500 strips away needless design details in lieu of being supremely legible, intensely robust and simply timeless.

children.text: Inspired by the first-ever successful summit of Mount Everest by Sir Edmund Hillary and his Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, who wore a Rolex Oyster Perpetual, the Rolex Explorer has long been Rolex's ultimate adventure watch. Constructed entirely from Rolex's 904L steel, the Explorer's robust design ensures that it can always battle the elements. Featuring some of Rolex's most capable movements and a rich heritage to boot, the Explorer is another display of their timeless design as this icon of watchmaking has remained virtually untouched in its aesthetic since its inception. Identifiable by its signature 3-6-9 glossy black dial, a flat stainless steel bezel, and entirely satin-brushed stainless steel case and bracelet, the Rolex Explorer has become renowned for its understated class, sporty elegance, and capable construction. New for 2023, Rolex expanded the Explorer collection with a new 40mm variant, the ref. 224720 in stainless steel. Offered here we have the ref. 224270 powered by the automatic cal. 3230 with 70 hours of power reserve that ensures the new Explorer has all of the horological might and provenance that one might expect in a modern release from the Genevan Giants.
THE DIAL
Boasting a glossy black dial, as always for the Explorer, the ref. 224270 features all of the Explorer's iconic dial elements, such as its applied indices and applied 3-6-9 Arabic numerals.
THE CONSTRUCTION

A familiar design on the wrist of Explorer aficionados, but with a new profile, the new ref. 224270 takes the Explorer's iconic and historic design, and jumps it from the 36mm and 39mm versions that we have seen in the past to a larger-than-ever 40mm.

Expanding the Explorer's current offering from the 36mm version with a new larger 40mm size that takes the icon's signature design and gives it the gravitas that a sports Rolex deserves, the ref. 224270 is an ultra-modern take on a classic.

children.text: Debuting in 1971, the Rolex Explorer II was released to satiate the demand for a relatively niche timepiece for a particular type of explorer, Spelunkers, or cave explorers as we may call them. Made only of steel, the Explorer II's construction ensures that none of its parts might crack or break off against a rock in cramped conditions, such as a bezel insert. With this use in mind, the Explorer II originally featured its iconic arrow-shaped 24-hour hand to differentiate between AP and PM for spelunkers that might lose track of the day and night cycle while they were in caves for days at a time. The modern Explorer II models have had this function exchanged for a fully operational GMT-hand. Featuring its signature fixed stainless-steel bezel, arrow-shaped 2nd hour hand, and robust design, the Explorer II makes for an incredible jack-of-all-trades timepiece as it comprises of just about everything your modern exploring needs might demand. Whether you're 500m under a mountain, 30m underwater, or 10,000m in the air on a trans-Atlantic flight, the Explorer II has you covered. Released in 2021 as a 50th anniversary launch and ushering in a new era for the Rolex Explorer II collection, the ref. 226570 slimmed down the Explorer II's 42mm dimensions through its slimmer lugs while retaining the iconic fan-favourite orange arrow-shaped GMT-hour hand. Boasting the collection's signature steel bezel with its distinctive radial brushed finish, the Explorer II is the perfect blend of Rolex's legendary tool watch-specific heritage and their modern focus on the luxurious aspects of watchmaking.
